cream-paper.$description: Cream Paper — Page background canvas, hero overlays, editorial section backdrops — the warm off-white that sets the entire system apart from generic SaaS grays

pure-white.$description: Pure White — Card surfaces, product UI mockups, input fields, text on dark photography

charcoal-ink.$description: Charcoal Ink — Primary text, strong borders, icon strokes, logo wordmark — the maximum-contrast voice

near-black.$description: Near Black — Body text and heading color for subtle warmth below pure black

pressed-graphite.$description: Pressed Graphite — Filled button backgrounds, dark UI surfaces, photo overlay scrims

slate.$description: Slate — Secondary text, subtle heading borders, metadata — the 60% voice

iron.$description: Iron — Dark borders and separators for elevated surfaces and inverted UI. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

stone.$description: Stone — Muted body text, caption-level copy, placeholder text

pewter.$description: Pewter — Hairline borders on low-emphasis elements, dividers

fog.$description: Fog — Hairline borders, subtle dividers, ghost outlines — the most frequent border color in the system

rules-font.$description: Editorial display face for all headings — the weight-500 medium is deliberately non-bold, creating a literary, hand-set quality rather than a SaaS marketing shout. Tight -0.02em letter-spacing at 69px tightens the large headline to a single confident line. Substitute: 'Söhne Breit', 'GT America', or 'Inter' at weight 500

ui-sans-serif.$description: System sans-serif for all functional text — body copy at 400/16px, UI labels and button text at 500, emphasized sub-labels at 600. The neutral system face keeps the interface quiet so the Rules Font headlines carry all the personality. Substitute: 'Inter', 'Söhne', or 'Geist'
